reviews.author: IMPmovies.on.Instagram
reviews.content:
This was completely bonkers, in both the best and worst ways. Imagine a wild mash-up of Ready or Not, Kill Bill, and Looney Tunes, with flashes of countless other films thrown into the mix. It’s chaotic, and doesn’t always land, but it’s never dull.

The trailer does a great job of hiding a key element that I genuinely didn’t see coming. That surprise is also where the “mixed results” come in. I won’t spoil it, but while it adds a layer of dark comedy to the blood-soaked mayhem, it also hinders the movie at times, especially in an ending that’s so over-the-top it’ll likely split audiences right down the middle.

Performances and special effects are a bit uneven, but the action is where the film really shines. The set pieces are inventive, fast-paced, and gleefully excessive, with bloodshed dialled up to ridiculous levels.

This feels like the kind of film that might improve on a second watch, once you know what you’re in for. For now, it lands as a fun, chaotic ride - 7/10 for now.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: This is another one of those films where the best bits are definitely in the trailers. We are quickly briefed that siblings “Asia” (Zazie Beetz) and “Maria” (Myha’la) are being abused by their father, but when the former adopts a more permanent solution to their problem, she is incarcerated and many years pass during which the sisters lose contact. Upon her release, “Asia” gets herself a job working as a cleaner in a grand looking New York skyscraper, but little does she appreciate just what services she will be required to provide to “Lily” (Patricia Arquette) and her coterie of staff and hedonistic residents. Luckily, she might be able to rely on “Ray” (Paterson Joseph) who is married to her new nemesis but who has become disillusioned with things - but even together, is there any chance they can combat their uniquely armed foes? I did quite like the last ten minutes, but otherwise this is all too familiar and predictable, with shades of a demonic version of “John Wick” running through most of it, and very little comedy once we establish the Hammer-style nature of the scenarios. I suppose it does look good, but I find these one person army features increasingly repetitive to watch and I felt this recycled itself once to often for me.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content: What his lacks in story it makes up for in visual flair and spectacle. The casting is solid, the action rightfully over the top and the direction very solid. The relationship between the two main protagonists is a bit convoluted, and hard to relate to, but the movie gets on well without their bond being that well worked out. The ending is fittingly bonkers. It is fun, if not the most substantial movie you will see.

reviews.author: Vinicius Monteiro
reviews.content:
Mixing survival horror with fast-paced martial arts usually gets fans excited, and "They Will Kill You" definitely delivers an undeniable visual punch in its first few minutes. Directed by Kirill Sokolov, the movie starts off strong with a Tarantino-meets-Raimi vibe, turning the luxurious Virgil skyscraper into a suffocating, claustrophobic arena. However, this frantic energy quickly burns out. The over-the-top stylization—which often feels like a visceral comic book or a fast-paced video game—starts to bury the actual tension, and the sense of real danger fades away.

The biggest issue comes from the movie's own fantastical premise. While the hand-to-hand combat is brutal and packed with great sound and visual design, the fights lose all their stakes because the cult members have instant regenerative powers. When a bad guy can just get up minutes after taking a lethal blow, completely intact and ready for round two, the desperate fight for survival turns into a repetitive cycle. The extreme violence stops being shocking and just goes on autopilot, draining the story of the genuine threat it needed to stay afloat.

Zazie Beetz is the absolute anchor of this movie. She delivers a magnetic, fiercely physical performance as Asia Reaves, perfectly balancing genuine panic with explosive rage as she desperately searches for her sister. She does the absolute most with the material she’s given, but the script just doesn't do her talent justice, leaving her character's emotional depth pretty shallow. Unfortunately, the rest of the cast suffers an even worse fate. Patricia Arquette is wasted as a one-dimensional villain who basically just hands out orders and sadistic smiles, while big names like Heather Graham and Tom Felton are literally and figuratively masked, reduced to immortal punching bags for the protagonist. It’s incredibly frustrating to see so much acting potential thrown away just to boost the movie's promotional posters.

Even the setting eventually loses its charm. The New York skyscraper initially offers a cool contrast between opulent luxury and gory carnage, but it quickly devolves into generic dark hallways and poorly lit rooms that add nothing to the suspense. The movie tries to shoot in all directions, attempting to blend the dark humor of "Ready or Not" with the frantic battles of "Kill Bill," but it fails to build a solid identity of its own. Even the social commentary about the elite sacrificing the working class for immortality feels totally superficial. It acts as a mere excuse to kick off the bloodbath rather than actually exploring the hypocrisy of the super-rich.

By the time the rushed, messy climax hits, the repetitive fights have already numbed the audience, making the final showdown feel convenient and unrewarding. It’s a classic case of a movie that had all the right pieces to be a genre standout but took the loud and shallow route instead. Still, if you're just looking to turn off your brain for an hour and a half and watch some mindless, uncompromised carnage, it definitely has its shock value. It is worth checking out just to feel the chaotic pacing Sokolov tries to create—and to see if the choices that fell flat for others might actually work for you. After all, the most honest metric for any movie is always your own experience watching it.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: An ex-convict takes a housekeeping job at a mysterious Manhattan high-rise to rescue her estranged sister, only to find herself battling a sadistic, immortal cult of wealthy satanists.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: After serving ten years in prison, Asia Reaves poses as a housekeeper at the Virgil, a prestigious NYC apartment building linked to mysterious disappearances, in order to track down her missing sister Maria. Upon arrival, she discovers that the building's wealthy elite are members of a satanic cult who achieve immortality through annual human sacrifices. Utilizing her lethal prison survival skills, Asia fights her way through floor after floor of murderous, supernatural tenants to save her sister and escape.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Ten years after taking the fall for shooting her abusive father, ex-convict Asia Reaves lands a maid job at the Virgil, an iconic 100-year-old New York high-rise. Asia goes undercover under the guise of an ordinary employee, but her true goal is to locate her estranged younger sister Maria, who works at the building and has gone missing among its sinister rumors. On her first night, masked intruders ambush Asia in her room, expecting an easy victim for their annual sacrificial ritual. However, her fierce combat skills forged in prison turn the tables on her attackers. Asia soon learns the horrifying truth: the Virgil's high-society residents are part of a demonic cult whose members become immortal by pledging their souls to a possessed entity. Reunited with Maria, Asia is shocked to find that her sister has voluntarily accepted the luxury of the building and is reluctant to leave. As the cult targets the sisters to complete their blood ritual, Asia wages a hyper-violent war against regenerating cultists using weapons ranging from shotguns to flaming axes. In a final floor showdown, Asia outsmarts the demonic entity, burns the magical ledger that grants the residents immortality, and destroys the cult once and for all.
aiEnrichment.synopsis:
Asia Reaves spent a decade behind bars protecting her younger sister, Maria, from their abusive upbringing. Freshly released and hardened by years of surviving in prison, Asia discovers that Maria has drifted away and taken a job at the Virgil—a grand, century-old Manhattan high-rise with a dark reputation for high-society scandals and unexplained disappearances. Determined to get her sister back, Asia secures a position as a housekeeper in the building under false pretenses.

It does not take long for Asia to realize that the Virgil's eccentric residents and staff harbor horrifying secrets. On her very first night in the building, she becomes the target of a sinister, organized hunt led by a group of wealthy tenants who intend to perform a horrific ritual. Unbeknownst to her attackers, Asia is far from a helpless victim; her combat experience makes her a force to be reckoned with against any threat.

Navigating the building's lavish, twisted floor plan, Asia must fight off waves of sadistic cultists while uncovering the dark, occult forces controlling the high-rise. Packed with grueling combat, dark comedic slapstick, and intense action, the story follows Asia's desperate ascent through the building to rescue her sister and survive the night against an unholy, bloodthirsty community.

story_structure.resolution: The violent ordeal reaches its end, leaving the survivor to process the harrowing secrets of the high-rise and face the aftermath of escaping the cult.
